clue.text: On the mountain, a camel? To a certain extent

definitions.text: On the mountain, a camel? To a certain extent

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
taken as written

indicators.note: only partly taking a word means keeping just its opening stretch of letters

parts.note: the opening two letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone spots a humped beast up in the hills and wonders whether it is a camel, of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: an ALPACA is a mountain-dwelling relative of the camel, so it is a camel to a certain extent.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpacas are South American camelids bred high in the Andes, close cousins of camels and llamas.

clue.text: Painful withdrawal, having raw meat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: abrupt, unpleasant stopping of a drug habit
second meaning: poultry served chilled rather than hot

explanation.surface: Someone suffering through a rough detox also has to eat uncooked flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: Raw is stretched a little: cold bird meat has not been freshly cooked and served hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard idiom for sudden total abstinence from an addictive substance, and literally a chilled holiday bird.

clue.text: Deserters run off endlessly going north, with this as their guide?

indicators.note: in a down entry, travelling north means reading from the bottom upwards
without an end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rats are said to desert a sinking ship
to elope is to run off secretly to marry

explanation.surface: Fleeing deserters head north at night, steering by a familiar star.
explanation.walkthrough: ELOPE loses its last letter to give ELOP, then RATS plus ELOP is read upwards. Fugitives heading north would indeed navigate by this star.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the north star, has long served travellers as a fixed reference point for finding north.

clue.text: Plain comfortable

definitions.meaning: second meaning: cosy, like being at home

explanation.definitionFit: In American use the word means unattractive, while in British use it means cosy and unpretentious, like a house.

clue.text: But is such a book easy-going?

definitions.text: But is such a book easy-going?

parts.words: But is such a book easy-going?
parts.note: surface reading: asking whether a certain volume makes light reading
setter's reading: the opposite of easy-going is a rigid spine, a stiff cover rather than soft

explanation.walkthrough: Easy-going suggests a relaxed person or a light read; the joke is that this kind of book has a stiff, unbending binding, so it is anything but easy-going.
explanation.definitionFit: A book bound in rigid boards is named for its stiff cover, contrasted with the floppy paperback edition.

clue.text: Now madam's potty as her!

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters go wildly out of order

parts.note: taken as written; the 's is the verb is

explanation.surface: A remark that the lady of the house has now gone as crazy as some other woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram letters themselves describe the answer: madam, now potty, is a MADWOMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points to a female person, and the clue as a whole says she is crazy.

clue.text: Jumper's game requiring nerve

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
neck means cheek or nerve, as in brazen boldness

explanation.surface: An athlete's sport demands courage.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper's looks like an athlete or horse; in British English a jumper is a sweater, and the 's is just is.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater with a high folded collar around the throat is a kind of British jumper.

clue.text: Go from the end of the bridge and cross it

indicators.note: the end means the final letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
a cross is the letter X
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to leave from the far side of a bridge and walk across.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave or depart from a place is a verb sense of the word, as in to quit a room.

clue.text: Thoughtful German issue

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the German word for child, issue meaning offspring

explanation.surface: A contemplative matter of debate in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue looks like a topic or problem, but here means offspring, as in die without issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerate people are generous and caring, and Kind is the everyday German noun for a child.

clue.text: Derail badly — having come off the line, you might?

definitions.text: having come off the line, you might?

indicators.note: done badly suggests the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A train jumps off its tracks, a bad derailment.
explanation.walkthrough: The line looks like a railway track after derail, but it is a telephone line that has been cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: After a phone call drops, a caller would naturally ring the same number again.

clue.text: Union head turns to Judaism

indicators.note: the word turns implies the letters are spun round into another order

parts.note: taken as written
Sion, a variant spelling of Zion, stands for the Jewish people and faith

explanation.surface: A trade union leader converts to the Jewish faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Union suggests a trade union with a head, but it is the definition: sticking together.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesion is the state of things being stuck or joined together, a physical uniting of surfaces.

clue.text: Financial instability of two supported couples, the first disheartened

indicators.note: the opening item has its heart, its central letter, taken out

parts.note: a bosom and a bust are each a pair held up by a bra

explanation.surface: Two married couples who rely on others fall into money trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Couples looks like married pairs; here the pairs are breasts. BOSOM loses its middle S to give BOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The economic cycle of rapid growth followed by collapse is a classic description of unstable markets.

clue.text: Fold of fat taking bottoms up, you might say?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sagging roll of flesh under the jaw

definitions.text: taking bottoms up, you might say?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: replacing one drinking toast with another said twice, chin-chin

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to a toast leads to a roll of fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottoms up and chin-chin are both drinking toasts; chin-chin is chin said twice, so the answer playfully describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose layer of flesh beneath the jaw, typical of overweight people, is commonly called this.

clue.text: A treat for which I yell out loud

indicators.note: said out loud means the words are heard as speech, not read

parts.note: to yell is to scream

explanation.surface: Something so good that I shout for it, echoing the rhyme 'I scream, you scream, we all scream for ice cream'.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dessert bought from a van on sunny days is a classic sweet indulgence.

clue.text: Germany needs a national prime minister

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
a citizen of Israel

explanation.surface: Germany requires a foreign premier.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli served twice as Conservative premier of Britain under Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Vineyard brews of the upper classes

parts.note: two brews: cha and tea are both words for tea
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Wines made by the aristocracy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Bordeaux a wine estate with its own grapes and winery is named this, as in Château Margaux.

clue.text: Make strong old men be refined

indicators.note: refining a material reprocesses it, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Toughen up elderly gentlemen and make them more cultured.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder includes be, which also reads as a linking verb in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone courage or confidence is to fortify them, making them bolder in spirit.

clue.text: A section of Ankara, China's Asian capital once

indicators.note: a section is just a slice of the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the Turkish city and the start of the country

explanation.surface: A district of Turkey's capital resembles China's capital in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: Ankara is itself a capital, which pulls attention there; the answer was Pakistan's capital until 1959.
explanation.definitionFit: Karachi served as the seat of Pakistan's government from independence until Islamabad replaced it.

clue.text: Shaky performer in call for ardency gone to pieces

parts.note: to bell someone is British slang for calling them on the phone

indicators.note: broken into pieces means the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nervous entertainer collapses under demands for passion.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaky suggests nervousness, but it describes a dancer who shakes her midriff.
explanation.definitionFit: This dancer performs a Middle Eastern style built on shimmying hips and abdomen, so shaking is the act.

clue.text: Sound of a fitful, yet brave, man

indicators.note: the sound of words means we hear them rather than spell them

parts.note: fitful means irregular or patchy

explanation.surface: A man who is both nervy and courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: Brave looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American warrior is traditionally called a brave, and the Apache are a people of the American Southwest.

clue.text: Unlimited wildlife expedition in a distant place

indicators.note: without limits means both boundary letters are removed

parts.note: a safari is a trip to see wild animals

explanation.surface: An endless safari to remote lands.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means far away or at a great remove, as in from afar.

clue.text: River is a river? Anything but!

parts.note: taken as written
R is the map abbreviation for river
an emphatic denial

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether a waterway is really a waterway, firmly rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: The question seems to deny the answer is a river, yet the answer is one: the Arno flows through Florence and Pisa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arno is the major waterway of Tuscany, flowing through Florence to the sea near Pisa.

clue.text: Something crude enters sheep, something hairy

indicators.note: going into something means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a flock is a group of sheep
ore is crude, unrefined metal-bearing rock

explanation.surface: Some rough material gets into the woolly animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Something hairy seems to describe the sheep, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock of hair growing above the brow is a tuft of hair, so a hairy thing.

clue.text: Cell door confines me

indicators.note: to confine is to hold within, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a gate is an outdoor door
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prison cell's door locks me in.
explanation.walkthrough: Cell door reads as prison, but cell is a biological one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sperm and egg are reproductive cells in biology, carrying half the chromosomes each.

clue.text: Country whose name was changed, so I heard

indicators.note: a name that has been changed has had its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that a nation was renamed.
explanation.walkthrough: So I heard looks like a sound-alike signal but is the fodder. Fittingly, the country really was renamed Zimbabwe in 1980.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was a former nation of southern Africa, the earlier name of present-day Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Greek character needs a doctor, one figures

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Greek person needs a doctor, someone reckons.
explanation.walkthrough: Figures reads as a verb, reckons, but is a plural noun: shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhombi are geometrical shapes, parallelograms with four equal sides, the plural of rhombus.
